what_it_is: Rolls-Royce plc is the UK aero-engine OEM whose military engines power the Indian Air Force's C-130J fleet (AE 2100D3) and heritage Hawk trainers (Adour, with HAL partnership). It runs an engineering centre in Bengaluru and a 700-seat global capability centre opened in 2025, making India both a fleet customer and an engineering base.
india_angle: Rolls-Royce's Indian footprint combines engine fleets (C-130J AE 2100D3, Hawk Adour via the Rolls-Royce/HAL partnership), Bengaluru engineering operations, and long-cycle component manufacturing partnerships with Indian industry. MRO and engineering expansion in Bengaluru deepened with the 2025 GCC opening.
intelligence_assessment: Corporate evidence is strong (OEM product pages, country-site content, business media). The Indian military thread worth tracking is C-130J engine MRO localisation and any Adour follow-on work as HAL's Hawk industrial role evolves.

faq.q: Which Indian aircraft use Rolls-Royce engines?
faq.a: The C-130J Super Hercules uses the AE 2100D3, and the Hawk trainer lineage uses the Adour engine produced with HAL participation.
